title: His parents, brothers and the family quarrel that sent him west
summary: His father was Everett Arlington Bunn, mother Elizabeth Jackson, brothers Roger and Kenneth; Kenneth's drunken cursing at their mother made him leave.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: There was some -- we were talking about some family history yesterday.
About who?
Also. And we didn't get that on tape. About your parents. Your father's name was?
Everett.
Everett Arlington Bunn.
Yeah.
And your mother's name was Elizabeth Jackson?
That's right.
And you had two brothers.
Kenneth and Roger. Roger was the oldest. Kenneth was the middle and I was the baby.
How much difference was there in age?
Oh, quite a bit of difference. I was the baby.
You were the baby by a good many years.
Yeah.
And the last you know, they're all back east.
They was.
Yeah. You said that there was some family squabbles between what, Kenneth and your parents?
Kenneth and my mother.
Oh, I see. That was one of the reasons why you came out to the coast?
That's the reason why I left home. I just

couldn't take it. Because he was going out and getting drunk and then cussing mother out. He'd come home. He got hooked up with some chick, and momma would tell him about it. Every time she got to talking to him about it, he'd cuss her out. I got mad at him and told him to get out. He missed me. If he'd really hit me, I don't know what would have happened to me, because he was kind of hefty as a young fellow, you know, and I was the baby. I was taking up for my mother and father. Me being at home, too.
Yeah.
And I was the only one that could hold it up right then, you know, so why let him come and spoil it.
Where was your older brother in this situation?
Roger was in Wantagh, Long Island.
He wasn't living there any more.
No.
You and Kenneth were both still living at home?
Yeah, uh-huh.
Or you used to be at home a lot.
Yeah.
